residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must have been ordinarily resident in Nunavut for at least one year immediately before the divorce application (Divorce Act, RSC 1985, c. 3, s.3(1)).

waitingPeriod.description: No mandatory waiting period after filing. The one-year separation must be complete before or at the time the divorce order is granted. Divorce Order effective 31 days after made (Divorce Act, s.12).

noFault.name: One-Year Separation
noFault.description: Spouses have lived separate and apart for at least one year immediately preceding the determination of the divorce application.

fault.name: Physical or Mental Cruelty
fault.description: The respondent has treated the applicant with physical or mental cruelty of such a kind as to render intolerable the continued cohabitation of the spouses.

terminology.maritalProperty: Family Property (Family Law Act, SNu 2012, c. 30)

legalCitations.description: Federal divorce statute — governs divorce proceedings in all provinces and territories
Nunavut statute — division of family property and support on marriage breakdown
Federal guidelines for calculating child support amounts

basic.name: Application for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding in the Nunavut Court of Justice

basic.name: Divorce Order
basic.description: Draft order to be submitted to court for signature by a judge

childSupportGuidelines.notes: Federal Child Support Guidelines apply. Nunavut is not a designated province, so federal tables are used directly.

spousalSupportGuidelines.notes: SSAG are advisory only. Spousal support also available under Family Law Act, SNu 2012, c. 30 and Divorce Act s.15.2.

effectiveDateRule: 31 days after the divorce order is made, unless the court varies the effective date or both parties waive the waiting period (Divorce Act, s.12).
certificateNote: A Certificate of Divorce may be obtained from the court office after the effective date of the Divorce Order (Divorce Act, s.12(7)).

filingFees.notes: Contact the Nunavut Court of Justice registry in Iqaluit for current filing fees. Fee waiver may be available for low-income parties.

courtNotes: The Nunavut Court of Justice is unique in Canada — it is the only single-level trial court in the country. It combines the jurisdiction of a superior court and a territorial court. Created in 1999 under the Nunavut Act (SC 1993, c. 28) when Nunavut separated from the Northwest Territories.
